style: Technical, possession-oriented African side under Vladimir Petkovic with abundant attacking talent. Builds patiently and overloads the final third through creative midfielders and pacey, skilful forwards.
recent_form: Back at the World Cup for the first time since 2014. Strong CAF qualification campaign carried by a deep pool of European-based attackers heading into the tournament.

key_players.name: Riyad Mahrez
key_players.note: Generational leader with 38 international goals; heading to what he calls his last World Cup, still the team's creative reference point.

key_players.name: Mohamed Amine Amoura
key_players.note: Wolfsburg attacker offering pace, movement and a sharp goal threat.

key_players.name: Amine Gouiri
key_players.note: Marseille forward providing a mobile, clinical focal point in attack.

key_players.name: Houssem Aouar
key_players.note: Al-Ittihad playmaker adding technical quality and creativity in the final third.

key_players.name: Fares Chaibi
key_players.note: Eintracht Frankfurt midfielder contributing energy and ball progression.

key_players.name: Ibrahim Maza
key_players.note: Bayer Leverkusen talent representing the new generation in midfield.

historical_news: Algeria back at the World Cup for the first time since 2014 under Vladimir Petkovic.
Drawn in Group J alongside defending champions Argentina, Austria and Jordan.
Riyad Mahrez, 35, says this is his last World Cup after 38 international goals.
Squad boasts deep European-based attacking talent including Amoura, Gouiri and Aouar.
Algeria one of the higher-ranked African sides at the tournament at 28th.

media_sentiment.label: positive
media_sentiment.summary: Upbeat given a talented squad and World Cup return, with focus on Mahrez's farewell, though the daunting group with Argentina tempers ambitions.
